title: Module quiz: From business need to a testable spec

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A feature must return a complete answer to a waiting user within two seconds. The team's design is a chain of five calls, each taking about one second. Which action fits best?

options.text: Stream the final stage so that its first words appear sooner for the person waiting
options.says: Ruled out because "streaming does not shorten the total time", and the requirement is for the complete answer.

options.text: Merge or remove stages until the summed time sits inside the budget
options.says: Chained calls add up, so the fix is to cut the sequence: "a requirement of two seconds rules out a five-call pipeline".

options.text: Request a higher usage plan from the provider so that each individual call runs faster
options.says: Ruled out because a higher tier "does not make one call finish sooner".

options.text: Move the whole pipeline to asynchronous batches, which are processed at half the price
options.says: Ruled out because a batch "is the right design when nobody is waiting", and a user is waiting.

origin.section: Latency: what you can and cannot tune

questions.stem: After a team swaps its model for a newer id, the support lead says the new one feels better. What should happen before release?

options.text: Rerun the fixed evaluation set on the candidate id and compare it with the acceptance rate
options.says: The maintain routine is to re-run the evaluation set against the new model and compare, so the change is judged on numbers.

options.text: Accept the lead's impression, since the replacement is the more recent release of the family
options.says: Ruled out because "a requirement that only a person's impression can settle is a wish".

options.text: Switch to the moving alias so that every later upgrade arrives without any change in the code
options.says: Ruled out because "a silent change of model is a silent change of behaviour".

options.text: Compare the monthly bill of the two models over a single representative week of production traffic
options.says: Ruled out because a bill covers cost alone, while the routine says to "re-run the evaluation set against the new model" for quality.

questions.stem: A feature runs comfortably under its entry-level request limit on average, but a quarterly campaign sends four times that rate for ten minutes, and the first requests of the burst are refused. Which response fits best?

options.text: Size for the highest peak, then ask for a bigger allowance or smooth the traffic
options.says: The bucket can be emptied by a burst whatever the average is, so the page asks for the peak and offers a higher tier or a smoother load.

options.text: Size for the daily average, because capacity refills continuously over each minute of the day
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "write the peak, not the mean".

options.text: Shorten every reply from the model so that each single request counts for less against the limit
options.says: Ruled out because "a request counts against the request limit however short its reply is".

options.text: Switch the residency setting to global so that a second and separate pool becomes available
options.says: Ruled out because "rate limits are shared across all geos", so no second pool appears.

questions.stem: A help site must answer visitors only from the company's own policy documents, one answer for each visitor, with the visitor waiting. Which design fits best?

options.text: Chain three separate calls that draft, check and polish the reply before it is shown
options.says: Ruled out because a chain is for "several dependent steps, each checkable", and three calls would also cost latency.

options.text: Run an agent loop that explores the documents until the loop is satisfied with what it found
options.says: Ruled out because an agent loop is for when "the path depends on what is found and cannot be listed in advance".

options.text: Fetch the matching passages, then ask once for a reply grounded in them
options.says: Answers that must come from the company's own documents point to retrieval followed by one call.

options.text: Submit each question as part of an overnight batch that is collected the next morning
options.says: Ruled out because a batch "is the right design when nobody is waiting".

origin.section: Matching an architecture to the requirement
